messages:
Marta (CS): Heads-up — LyricHealth dropped to ~10% of their normal API calls this morning. Saw a big dip starting ~02:00 UTC. Noticed a note about a new interim CTO and a competitor trial in their procurement thread.
Kevin (AM): Ugh. Which competitor? any names?
Marta (CS): They mentioned NimbusAI in the procurement email. Also flagged that the new interim CTO (Raj) wants a security/latency deep dive before committing.
Zane (Solutions): I pulled usage traces. Their prod key (lyric-p-key) shows: 
```
2026-03-20T01:30:00Z -> 420 req/min
2026-03-20T02:00:00Z -> 38 req/min
2026-03-20T02:15:00Z -> 12 req/min
2026-03-20T03:00:00Z -> 8 req/min
```
Seems like a gating change rather than a gradual drop.
Samir (Support): No errors in our side. No 4xx/5xx spike. Auths succeeding. Could be client-side throttling or a new proxy rule from Lyric. I pinged their SRE via email.
Marta (CS): I replied to Raj and asked for a 30-min sync. Asked for any security checklist items they require and whether Nimbus did anything special (e.g., on-prem bundle).
Kevin (AM): Can we get a 1-pager on our security posture + quick perf snapshot for their region? Raj tends to escalate to procurement if it’s not clear.
Zane (Solutions): I can assemble: SOC2 summary, TLS/KMS notes, and a 1-slide latency heatmap. Also include a comparison: hosted vs dedicated latency profile for their request sizes.
Marta (CS): Perfect. Also suggest we offer a short-canary dedicated node for 48h (discounted) to show stable latency — low friction proof. Raj might like an isolated environment.
Samir (Support): If we spin a sample dedicated pool, I’ll add tracing hooks and a one-click rollback policy. Need confirmation from infra though.
Kevin (AM): I'll loop in infra and pricing. Marta — can you draft the outreach to Raj that offers the 48h canary + 30-min session this week? I can cc procurement.
Marta (CS): Drafted message and pasted below — please tweak: 
"Hi Raj — congrats on the new role. We noticed a sharp drop in LyricHealth traffic and saw Nimbus running a short pilot. Would you be open to a 30-min call this week to review security and latency? We can stand up an isolated 48-hour dedicated canary with tracing so your SREs can validate in your environment. Happy to share SOC2 docs and a short latency report ahead of time. — Marta"
Zane (Solutions): LGTM. Add ability to run a small prompt set they choose so we show representative p99 behavior.
Samir (Support): Also add a note: we can enable request-level debugging flags for the canary (redacted tokens) so they can replay traces privately.
Marta (CS): Sent to Raj and CC'd Kevin + Samir. ops-bot:tracking created-ticket LY-8342 for the canary request.
ops-bot: Ticket LY-8342 created (owner: Samir). Due: 2026-03-22.
Kevin (AM): Good. Keep this thread for updates. If Raj declines, next move is a targeted executive QBR with procurement.
Marta (CS): Agreed. Will post Raj's response here. For reference: bringing in Nimbus intel: procurement note said Nimbus offered an on-prem connector and a 6-week pilot. That may be the gating factor.
Zane (Solutions): If on-prem is the ask, we should surface our Private deployment checklist and timeline (2-4 weeks typical). But show the 48h dedicated canary first to buy time.
Samir (Support): Will stand by to provision tracing and the canary once infra thumbs-up.
Marta (CS): Update 2h later — Raj replied: "Appreciate the reach-out. Let's do the 30-min tomorrow 15:00 UTC. Security wants SOC2 + encryption details now." I attached Zane's doc draft.
Kevin (AM): Win. Prep notes for the meeting and line up a short demo for the canary flow.
Marta (CS): Cool — I'll confirm meeting and share materials. Closing loop here once meeting happens.
